question.problem: Consider $E=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ and a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ Find the row operation that, when applied to $A,$ is equivalent to multiplying $A$ by the given elementary matrix $E$ from the left.
question.worked_solution:
The given matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the first row of ${I}_{3}$ by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary 
row operation ${R}_{1}:=5{R}_{1}$ to $A.$
